ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Old Woman Burns the Hermitage names the whole encounter among the old woman, the young woman, and the hermitage-dweller, not only its final fire.
EvidenceBody: In its repeated narrative, an old woman supports a hermitage-dweller for twenty years and sends a young woman to attend him. The young woman embraces him and asks, ‘at just such a time, how is it?’ He answers, ‘a withered tree leans against a cold cliff; through the three winter months there is no warmth.’ On hearing the report, the old woman says that for twenty years she has supported only a common fellow, drives him out, and burns the hermitage. Later masters cite, verse, question, and re-appraise the case: one asks why various quarters support the recorded questioner; another proposes that the hermitage-dweller should have laughed when approached; another says that to uphold the school and establish the teaching requires such a person, speaking of the old woman. These opposed recorded appraisals belong to the case's reception; this entry does not decide between them.
